title: Reading or changing another user's bot through X-Bot-Id
description: The admin API selects the bot from the X-Bot-Id header.

evidence.description: Bot must belong to the session user; otherwise 403.

reason: Ownership is checked for every admin request; tests cover status, config, logs and chunks for foreign, platform, expired and empty ids (all 403).

title: Chunk and vector ids used only 8 characters of the file id
description: Chunk rows and vectors were keyed `${fileId.slice(0,8)}-${idx}` and written with INSERT OR REPLACE / upsert. With many bots, two uploads sharing the 32-bit prefix would overwrite each other's chunk rows, keyword rows and vectors across tenants.
root_cause: Ids were not globally unique once documents from many tenants share one table and index.
intended_behavior: Every chunk id is unique across all bots, and keyword-index deletes are bot-scoped.

conditions.description: Two documents whose random file ids share the first 8 hex characters (birthday bound ~65k uploads).

execution.attacker_perspective: Any user uploading documents; the collision is not attacker-chosen.
payloads: Two uploads with colliding id prefixes
instructions: Reason from source: INSERT OR REPLACE on a shared id replaces the other bot's row.
execution.observed_result: Source-confirmed overwrite path; fixed by using the full id.

remediation.strategy: Use the full file UUID in chunk and vector ids and scope FTS deletes by bot_id.

code_changes.fixed_code: id: `${file.id}-${startIdx + i}`; DELETE FROM chunks_fts WHERE chunk_id = ? AND bot_id = ?

impact.reason: Silent cross-tenant overwrite of document chunks.

title: Failed sign-ins could lock every account out
description: The sign-in throttle kept a single global counter (100 failures per 10 minutes) shared by every login. Once accounts existed, anyone failing logins from a handful of IPs could make all sign-ins, for every user, return 429.
root_cause: The global failure counter protecting the platform-admin password was also applied to every account sign-in.
intended_behavior: Guessing is limited per IP and per targeted e-mail; a global lock applies only to the single platform-admin password.

evidence.description: Fixed: per-IP and per-email counters for accounts; 'lf:<slot>:all' only when scope.platform

conditions.description: Unauthenticated network clients from about 13 IPs.

instructions: Fail 9 logins for one e-mail from different source IPs, then sign in as another user.
execution.observed_result: After the fix the targeted e-mail is locked (429, even with the right password) while another account signs in (200).

remediation.strategy: Scope counters: per IP always, per e-mail for accounts, global only for the platform-admin password.

likelihood.reason: Needs only a few source IPs.

impact.reason: Every user loses dashboard access for the lock window; no data exposure.

confidence.reason: Covered by a local Worker test with distinct cf-connecting-ip values.

title: One free account could exhaust the platform's shared Workers AI budget
description: User bots without their own Gemini key embed documents and run owner test chats on the platform's Workers AI. Before the fix, ingestion had no per-bot size cap beyond 2,000 chunks and no platform-wide embedding budget, and /api/admin/test-chat was not counted in any daily quota, so one signed-up user could spend the free neuron allowance shared with every other user and the demo bot.
root_cause: Work done for user bots on the platform's AI binding was not metered against a platform-level budget.
intended_behavior: Each user bot is bounded, and all user bots together cannot spend more than a configured daily share of the platform's AI budget.

trace.description: Any signed-in user can upload chunks for their own bot.
No platform-wide metering existed before the fix (now spendPlatform).
Chunks are embedded on the platform's Workers AI binding when the bot has no Gemini key.

evidence.description: Fixed: owner tests counted with dailyQuota(..., bot)

execution.attacker_perspective: A registered user with up to 3 bots.
instructions: Run the Worker locally, sign in as a seeded user, create a document and post chunks past the cap.
execution.observed_result: After the fix the request is rejected with 413 before any embedding (Playwright: 'user bots cannot index oversized documents').

remediation.strategy: Cap user-bot documents at 400 chunks, meter Workers AI embeddings for all user bots in a daily D1 counter, and count owner test chats in the bot's daily quota.

code_changes.fixed_code: if (startIdx + n > USER_BOT_MAX_CHUNKS) return 413; if (embedder !== 'gemini' && !(await spendPlatform(env, 'emb:all-users', n, platformDailyEmbeds(env)))) return 429;

likelihood.reason: Sign-up is open to anyone and needs no payment.

impact.reason: Denial of AI answers for every tenant until the daily allowance resets; no data exposure.

confidence.reason: Source path is direct and the fixed limit is covered by a local Worker test.

title: Sign-up reveals whether an e-mail is registered
description: Sign-up returns 409 for an existing e-mail.
reason: Accepted product trade-off without a crossed boundary: sign-up is limited to 5 per IP per day, sign-in uses one message and equal PBKDF2 work for unknown e-mails.

title: Vectorize metadata filtering for vectors written before the 'bot' index existed
description: Tenant filtering in Vectorize uses metadata.bot, which requires a metadata index. Vectors upserted before the index is created are not filterable.
claimed_root_cause: Metadata index creation order on an existing index.

evidence.description: Defence in depth: candidates re-checked with WHERE bot_id = ? in D1, so foreign vectors can never become passages.

blockers: Vectorize filtering behaviour is not observable locally (the binding only runs remotely).

validation_plan.local: Not available; D1 re-check is covered by the cross-tenant chat test.
validation_plan.deployment: After deploy, the workflow creates the 'bot' metadata index and the platform document is re-indexed; confirm with an owner-observed query that only that bot's vectors return.

title: User bots spending the platform's provider keys
description: Provider keys can come from Worker secrets.

trace.description: Strips provider secrets for non-platform bots.

evidence.description: tenantEnv removes GEMINI_API_KEY, HF_TOKEN, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, ... for user bots.

reason: All model and embedding calls for a bot use tenantEnv; a test confirms the platform's HF secret is 'configured' for the platform bot and absent for a user bot.
